_meta.description: Florida roofing cost calculator inputs and multipliers. Planning only — not bids. Base dollar bands come from fl-cost-ranges.json (projectType roofing × size→scale).

disclaimer: Planning only — not a bid or contractor quote. These ranges are conceptual Florida planning bands for homeowner budgeting. They are not contractor-specific prices, guarantees, or formal estimates.
methodologyNote: Start from statewide Florida roofing bands by approximate roof/home size, then apply relative multipliers for system type, stories/access, and pitch/complexity. Multipliers are relative planning factors, not market quotes. Location (ZIP/city) is for contractor matching only and does not invent local prices.
floridaNotes: Wind-mitigation details, secondary water barriers, and product approvals often move Florida reroof costs as much as the visible surface material.
Coastal exposure, HOA rules, and impact or high-wind product choices can raise both material and labor time.
Insurance claims and policy renewal upgrades are separate from this planning tool — confirm coverage and requirements with your carrier.
Permitting and inspection cycles vary by jurisdiction; multi-story and complex roofs usually need more coordination time.

sizeOptions.label: Smaller roof / compact home
sizeOptions.description: Roughly a smaller single-family footprint or simple partial reroof
sizeOptions.proxyHint: Often ~1,200–1,800 sq ft living area or a modest roof square count

sizeOptions.label: Typical Florida home
sizeOptions.proxyHint: Often ~1,800–2,800 sq ft living area · full tear-off common

sizeOptions.label: Large or multi-wing home
sizeOptions.description: Bigger footprint, more squares, or larger multi-story shell
sizeOptions.proxyHint: Often ~2,800+ sq ft living area or a sprawling roof plan

materialOptions.label: Architectural asphalt shingles
materialOptions.explain: Shingles are the baseline planning system for most Florida homes.

materialOptions.label: Premium / impact-rated shingles
materialOptions.explain: Premium or impact-oriented shingles usually sit above standard architectural products.

materialOptions.label: Metal (standing seam or quality panels)
materialOptions.description: Higher material and detail labor than shingles
materialOptions.explain: Metal systems typically raise both material cost and install labor versus shingles.

materialOptions.label: Concrete or clay tile
materialOptions.description: Heavy system — structure and underlayment matter
materialOptions.explain: Tile is often among the highest planning bands due to weight, labor, and underlayment detail.

materialOptions.label: Low-slope / membrane (TPO, modified, etc.)
materialOptions.description: Common on Florida additions and low-slope sections
materialOptions.explain: Low-slope membrane work can be comparable to shingles mid-band but ranges widely with detailing.

storiesOptions.label: One story · easy access
storiesOptions.description: Single story, driveway staging, typical lot
storiesOptions.explain: Single-story access usually keeps labor and staging toward the lower side of the band.

storiesOptions.label: Two story · typical
storiesOptions.explain: Two-story height is treated as the neutral access assumption for planning.

storiesOptions.label: Multi-story or difficult access
storiesOptions.description: Tall work, tight lot, limited parking, or HOA staging limits
storiesOptions.explain: Height and tight access raise labor time, equipment needs, and disposal logistics.

pitchOptions.label: Simple geometry
pitchOptions.explain: Simple shapes cut labor hours and waste versus cut-up roofs.

pitchOptions.label: Moderate complexity
pitchOptions.explain: A typical Florida suburban roof shape is the mid planning assumption.

pitchOptions.label: Complex / steep / many details
pitchOptions.description: Steep pitch, many valleys, dormers, or transitions
pitchOptions.explain: Complex geometry and steeper pitches increase labor, waste, and safety/setup costs.

education: Roof size (squares) and system type are usually the two largest planning levers.
Tear-off layers, deck repairs, and underlayment package can move a job inside the band without changing the roof material.
This calculator does not price insurance claims, code upgrades after inspection, or structural repairs discovered mid-job.
